question: How many days of paternity leave do I get for a baby born in August 2025?
answer: 10 Working Days within six months, in up to two spells (Circular HR/CIR/2025/07, effective 1 July 2025), not the 5 Working Days in Clause 6.4.1.

evidence.quote: entitled to paternity leave of 5 Working Days
is increased from 5 Working Days to 10 Working Days

question: Can I add a casual leave day to my earned leave?
answer: Yes from 1 October 2025: Circular HR/CIR/2025/11 allows CL to be prefixed or suffixed to EL if the combined spell is at most 10 Working Days (sandwich rule applies). Clause 5.2 (no combination) is amended. CL still cannot be combined with Sick Leave.

evidence.quote: CL shall not be prefixed or suffixed to EL or Sick Leave
Casual Leave may be prefixed or suffixed to Earned Leave, provided that the combined spell does not exceed 10 Working Days

question: My grandmother passed away. Can I take bereavement leave?
answer: No. Bereavement leave covers only Immediate Family, defined in Clause 2.8 as spouse, children, parents and legal guardian; grandparents are excluded (confirmed by Circular HR/CIR/2026/02). Use CL or EL.

evidence.quote: Immediate Family does not include parents-in-law, siblings, grandparents or any other relative
continues to be unavailable on the death of a grandparent, sibling or parent-in-law

question: I am still on probation. How much maternity leave can I get?
answer: Clause 6.2.3 says 12 weeks for a Probationer, but Clause 1.5 says a more favourable statute prevails; under the Maternity Benefit Act as stated in Clause 6.2.1-6.2.2, a woman who has worked at least 80 days in the preceding 12 months is entitled to 26 weeks (12 weeks if two or more surviving children).

evidence.quote: A Probationer shall be eligible for maternity leave of 12 weeks only
provides a benefit more favourable to the Employee than this Policy, the statutory benefit shall prevail
has actually worked for the Company for not less than eighty days

question: I am an L2 associate. Can I encash my earned leave this year?
answer: No. Encashment during service is only for Grades L3 to L8 (Clause 4.4, Table 1). An L2 can carry EL forward up to 45 days; it is encashed on separation.

evidence.quote: Employees in Grades L1 and L2 are not eligible for encashment during service

question: Can an L4 employee take a sabbatical?
answer: Ordinarily no (Clause 8.3: Grade L5 and above), but the carve-out in Annexure D, D.6 allows an L4 with 5 years' Continuous Service admitted to a Company-sponsored full-time postgraduate programme to take up to six months with BU Head and CPO approval.

evidence.quote: An Employee in Grade L5 and above who has completed five years of Continuous Service
an Employee in Grade L4 with at least five years of Continuous Service who has been admitted to a full-time postgraduate programme sponsored by the Company

question: I am an L6 manager and worked last Sunday. Do I get a comp off?
answer: No. Compensatory off is only for Grades L1 to L4 (Clause 7.3); Grades L5 to L8 are not eligible.

evidence.quote: Employees in Grades L5 to L8 are not eligible for compensatory off

question: Can I donate some of my earned leave to a colleague who is ill?
answer: Not covered by the documents; the bot must say so and offer an HR ticket (Policy Clarification).

question: The Employee Handbook says paternity leave is 5 days. Is that right?
answer: No. The Handbook (Clause 6.2) is a summary dated 1 April 2025. The Leave Policy governs leave and Circular HR/CIR/2025/07 raised paternity leave to 10 Working Days within six months from 1 July 2025. The Handbook's own hierarchy (Clause 1.3) says the specific policy and the circular prevail.

is increased from 5 Working Days to 10 Working Days
the specific policy on a subject prevails over this Handbook, which is only a summary

question: I am an L7 senior manager. How much referral bonus will I get if my friend joins at L5?
answer: None. Employees in Grades L7 and L8 are not eligible for a referral bonus (Handbook Clause 11.3). For other eligible referrers an L5 hire carries Rs. 50,000 (Table 6).

evidence.quote: Employees in Grades L7 and L8

question: How much day-care reimbursement can I claim in Pune?
answer: Rs. 10,000 a month per child (up to two children aged six months to six years) from 1 September 2025 under Circular HR/CIR/2025/09; Clause 8.2 still shows the old Rs. 8,000.

evidence.quote: reimbursement of the fees of a registered day-care centre of up to Rs. 8,000 a month
is increased from Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 10,000 a month for each child

question: Does Nexora pay for egg freezing?
answer: Not covered by the documents; the bot must say so and offer an HR ticket (Benefits).

question: I am a male employee. Can I file a sexual harassment complaint with the Internal Committee?
answer: Yes, from 8 March 2026. Clause 2.2 limits the procedure to women (as in the Act), but Circular HR/CIR/2026/04 extends the complaint, inquiry, interim relief and non-retaliation provisions to Employees of all genders as Company policy; statutory remedies and appeals under the Act remain available only to women.

evidence.document: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
evidence.quote: The complaint and inquiry procedure under this Policy is available to women, as provided in the Act

evidence.document: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)

question: A colleague keeps sending me inappropriate messages on WhatsApp late at night. That is not at work, so does the POSH policy apply?
answer: Yes. The POSH Policy's definition of Workplace (Clause 3.10) includes messaging applications and groups used by colleagues, on any device and outside working hours; Annexure C, C.1 gives this exact example.

evidence.document: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)

question: A vendor gave me a Rs. 3,000 Amazon gift card for Diwali. Can I keep it?
answer: No. Since 1 August 2025 (Circular HR/CIR/2025/08) gift cards and other cash equivalents may not be accepted in any amount, and the Gift limit was cut from Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 2,000. Clause 6.2 (which allowed gift cards up to Rs. 5,000) is amended.

evidence.quote: including a gift card or voucher within that value
gift cards, vouchers, prepaid cards and other cash equivalents may not be accepted in any amount

question: Something happened with a colleague six weeks ago. The Code of Conduct says harassment must be reported within 30 days. Is it too late to complain to the Internal Committee?
answer: No. The Code (Clause 12.4) says 30 days, but sexual harassment complaints are governed by the POSH Policy and the Act: three months from the incident (or the last incident), extendable by three more months (POSH Clause 6.2). The statute and the specific policy prevail; the Code itself (Clause 1.3) defers to the POSH Policy.

evidence.quote: shall be reported to the HR Business Partner or the appropriate committee within 30 days of the incident

evidence.document: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
evidence.quote: within three months from the date of the incident
governs complaints of sexual harassment

question: I am an L4 developer and want to buy Nexora shares. Do I need pre-clearance?
answer: No pre-clearance or trading window restriction applies unless you are a Designated Person (all L8; L6-L7 in Finance, Legal, Secretarial, Investor Relations, Strategy; or notified). But no Employee may trade while holding UPSI (Clause 8.2, 8.5).

evidence.quote: every Employee in Grade L8; every Employee in Grades L6 and L7 in the Finance, Legal, Company Secretarial, Investor Relations and Strategy functions
Employees who are not Designated Persons do not need pre-clearance and are not bound by the Trading Window

question: My father-in-law is a director at one of our vendors. Do I need to declare it?
answer: Yes. Under the Code, Relative includes parents-in-law (Clause 2.6), which is wider than Immediate Family in the Leave Policy. Declare on the NPP within 15 days and do not take part in decisions about that vendor (Clauses 4.2, 4.6).

evidence.quote: and the Employee's parents-in-law
wider than the definition of Immediate Family used in the Leave Policy

question: I am an L2. What is my group medical insurance sum insured?
answer: Rs. 4,00,000 family floater from the 1 July 2025 renewal (Circular HR/CIR/2025/06); Table 5 still shows Rs. 3,00,000 for L1 to L3. Room rent limit 1 per cent, i.e. Rs. 4,000 per day.

evidence.quote: is increased from Rs. 3,00,000 to Rs. 4,00,000

question: I rent a flat in Bengaluru. Is Bengaluru a metro city for my HRA exemption?
answer: No. For HRA exemption the Compensation Policy defines Metro City as Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai only (Clause 2.6), so the limit in Bengaluru is 40 per cent of Basic Salary, even if Bengaluru is treated as a metro for other purposes such as travel.

evidence.quote: among the Company's locations only Chennai is a Metro City for house rent allowance
the limit for an Employee paying rent in Bengaluru is 40 per cent of Basic Salary

question: I resigned on 10 May. Will I get my variable pay for last year in the June salary?
answer: No. Variable pay is paid only to Employees on the rolls who have not resigned on or before the Payout Date (Clause 8.4); the exceptions (death, disability, retirement, Company-initiated termination not for misconduct or performance, Clause 8.5) do not include resignation (Annexure C, C.2).

evidence.quote: who has not resigned or been given notice of termination on or before that date
they do not cover resignation

question: Why is no professional tax deducted from my salary? I work in Noida.
answer: Uttar Pradesh does not levy professional tax on salaried employees, so none is deducted for Noida-based Employees (Clause 4.4, Table 2); other locations have State professional tax.

evidence.quote: No professional tax is deducted for Employees based in Noida, because Uttar Pradesh does not levy professional tax on salaried employees

question: I am an L4 on hybrid work. Can I choose Wednesday as one of my work-from-home days?
answer: No. From 1 October 2025 (Circular HR/CIR/2025/10), Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday are anchor office days for Grades L1 to L6, so Remote Work Days can only be Monday and Friday. Clause 5.2 (days agreed with the manager) no longer applies to L1-L6; L7-L8 still agree days with their manager.

evidence.document: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy

question: I am an L2 and worked 6 hours of approved overtime. At what rate will I be paid?
answer: Clause 9.3 says 1.5 times the Ordinary Rate of Wages, but Clause 1.3 says the State Shops and Establishments law requires twice the ordinary rate and that the law prevails. So overtime is paid at twice the ordinary rate (for the Clause 9.6 example, Rs. 250 x 2 x 6 = Rs. 3,000, not Rs. 2,250).

evidence.document: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy
evidence.quote: Overtime is paid at one and a half times the Ordinary Rate of Wages

evidence.document: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy
evidence.quote: requires Overtime to be paid at twice the ordinary rate of wages

question: I am an L6 manager on the US night shift. How much shift allowance do I get?
answer: None. Shift allowance is only for Grades L1 to L5 (Clause 6.2); Grades L6 to L8 are not eligible. (For L1-L5 the Night Shift rate is Rs. 650 per day from 1 June 2026 under Circular HR/CIR/2026/06.)

evidence.document: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy
evidence.quote: Employees in Grades L6 to L8 are not eligible for shift allowance

question: I am an L2. My flight lands at 11:30 p.m. Can I take an Uber home and claim it?
answer: Yes. From 15 November 2025, Circular HR/CIR/2025/12 lets any Grade use an app-based cab (standard category) for airport or station transfers between 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. and claim the actual fare without the Rs. 750 limit. Clause 7.1 otherwise limits L1-L3 to bus, metro or pooled cab up to Rs. 750.

question: I am an L2. Can I fly from Bengaluru to Chennai for a client meeting?
answer: Normally no. For journeys of 500 km or less, L1-L3 travel by AC 3-tier rail or AC bus (Clause 4.2, Table 1); Bengaluru-Chennai is about 350 km (Annexure C, C.2). The Reporting Manager may approve air travel only if no suitable train or bus gets you there in time.

evidence.quote: For journeys of 500 km or less, Employees in Grades L1 to L3 travel by rail in AC 3-tier or by air-conditioned bus

question: What is the hotel limit for an L5 staying in Mumbai?
answer: Rs. 6,000 per night excluding taxes, from 1 February 2025 (Circular HR/CIR/2025/01); Table 2 still shows Rs. 5,000 for L4-L5 in a Metro City.

evidence.quote: is increased from Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 6,000 per night, excluding taxes

question: I am an L5 leaving with 52 days of earned leave. How many days will be encashed in my full and final settlement?
answer: 45 days. The Separation Policy (Clause 8.1) says a maximum of 30 days, but the Leave Policy (Clause 11.2) encashes up to the Grade accumulation limit (45 for L5) and states (Clause 11.5, via 1.4) that it prevails over a different limit in the Separation Policy. The Separation Policy itself (Clause 1.3) says payments follow the policy governing each payment.

question: What is the notice period if I resign at L5?
answer: 90 days (Separation Policy Clause 5.1, Table 1). The Employee Handbook table shows 60 days for L3 to L5, but the Separation Policy governs notice periods and prevails (Separation Clause 1.3; Handbook Clause 1.3). 15 days if still on probation.

L3 to L5 60 days

question: I am an L3 with 60 days' notice. Can I buy out the whole notice period and leave next week?
answer: No. Since 15 April 2025 (Circular HR/CIR/2025/04) buyout is limited to 50 per cent of the Notice Period, so an L3 must serve at least 30 days unless the Company waives the rest (Clause 5.3). Clause 5.4 (buyout of the whole period) is amended.

evidence.quote: may buy out the whole or any part of the unserved Notice Period
an Employee may buy out not more than 50 per cent of the Notice Period

question: I left on 31 March after seven years. When must my gratuity be paid?
answer: Within 30 days of becoming payable (the Payment of Gratuity Act, as stated in Compensation Policy Clause 7.3), not the 45 days in Separation Policy Clause 8.2; the Separation Policy itself (Clause 1.3) says a more favourable statutory time limit prevails. Interest is payable on delay.

evidence.quote: Gratuity, where payable, is paid together with the F&F within the same 45 days
within 30 days of the date it becomes payable
